newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: More dead found in wake of Czech flooding.
newsitem.headline: More dead found in wake of Czech flooding.

text.p: Floods that have ravaged the eastern Czech Republic for more than a week receded further in many areas on Monday but emergency teams found more bodies in their wake, raising the death toll to 31.
Rescuers sifting through collapsed homes in the town of Troubky on the Becva river found eight dead, including an older couple, the national CTK news agency said.
Surging waters from torrential rain caused the worst flooding in the region this century. Flooding from the same general weather system in neighbouring Poland has killed a reported 35 people there.
The floods covered low-lying areas of the eastern third of the Czech Republic and parts of Poland, Austria and Slovakia, forcing tens of thousands from their homes.
The Morava river continued to rise in the southeastern Czech Republic on Monday, but the situation was improving further upstream.

Hundreds of people living close to the Morava in the Czech town of Hodonin were moved to higher ground on Sunday as the flood wave pushed slowly downstream, but it had yet to reach the town by midday on Monday.

CTK quoted a rescue official from Troubky, a town of 2,000 residents and 700 homes, as saying that 150 dwellings had been destroyed. An estimated 290 Czech villages and 50 cities and towns have been damaged in the flooding.
Financial damage estimates vary widely and Czech officials say it is far too early to make definitive forecasts.

An official from the Plzen-based engineering group Skoda a.s. told CTK that the company expected total damage in the region should range between 50 billion and 100 billion crowns ($1.46 billion and $2.9 billion).

An official for the largest Czech insurer, Ceska Pojistovna, told the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny that a rough estimate of that firm's exposure to the flood damage was about five billion crowns.
The Agriculture Ministry said on Friday preliminary estimates showed crop damage of about 1.4 billion crowns, with about 130,000 hectares of agricultural land affected.
Specific breakdowns for crops affected were not yet available.
The Prague government has allocated more than 10 billion crowns in aid to afflicted regions, financed partly by domestic bond issues of up to five billion crowns.

The Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s., a unit of Volkswagen AG, suspended production of its flagship Felicia hatchback last Wednesday because of a lack of supplies from firms in the flood zone. ($ = 34.13 Czech Crowns)
